I need an exec summary of the report below for Olivia Grant, our COO. She's choosing between the two finalist vendors at the ops review on Oct 29 and won't read the full thing. Paste-ready email body please.

---
Warehouse Management System Replacement: Vendor Evaluation
Prepared by: Ops Systems (Ravi Menon, Jo Alvarez), with input from Finance and IT Security
Draft v3, Oct 14

1. Background
Our current WMS (in-house, built 2014) runs 4 distribution centres. Support for its database version ends June 30 next year. Pick rate has been flat at about 92 lines/hr/picker for 3 years, while peers report 110 to 130. We sent an RFP to 7 vendors in July. 5 responded and 2 were shortlisted after demos: Stackline and Corvane.

2. Method
Weighted scoring: functional fit 35%, total cost 25%, implementation risk 20%, vendor viability 10%, security 10%. Each DC manager scored the demos independently.

3. Scores
Stackline 78/100, Corvane 74/100. Most of the gap is functional fit (Stackline 31/35 vs Corvane 26/35). Corvane scored higher on cost (22/25 vs 17/25).

4. Costs (5-year TCO)
Stackline: licence $410k/yr, implementation $1.2M, internal staff time est. $380k. 5-yr TCO approx $3.63M.
Corvane: licence $290k/yr, implementation $950k, internal staff time est. $520k (more custom ERP integration). 5-yr TCO approx $2.92M.
Stackline's quote is valid until Nov 15. Corvane's states no expiry. Neither includes the handheld scanner refresh (~$240k, needed either way).

5. Timeline
Stackline: DC1 live in 7 months, all 4 DCs in 11. Corvane: DC1 in 9 months, all in 14. Both need signature by mid-Nov to start in December. Corvane's 14 months runs past the June 30 database end of support for 3 DCs. IT says extended support can be bought but has not priced it.

6. Risks
Stackline: smaller (approx 180 staff), raised a Series C in March. Two references praised the product, but one said its go-live slipped 2 months. Peak-season support uses a partner we have not vetted.
Corvane: larger (approx 2,000 staff), stable. ERP integration is the main risk. Their connector for our ERP version is in beta. One reference on our ERP said integration took twice as long as planned.
Both: neither has deployed with our cold-storage configuration (DC3), which handles about 18% of volume.

7. Security
Both passed our questionnaire. Stackline has SOC 2 Type II. Corvane has ISO 27001, with a SOC 2 report due Q1.

8. Open items
- Extended DB support cost (IT, no date)
- Whether DC3 goes first or last (DC managers disagree)
- Stackline partner vetting (procurement, est. 3 weeks)
- Legal review of both MSAs not started
---

Annual Application Security Review, Northwind Platform
Conducted by: Halvard Security (external), Sept 8 to Sept 26, with internal AppSec (Priya Raman)
Report date: Oct 10

Scope: customer web app, public API, mobile apps, admin console, CI/CD pipeline. Out of scope: data warehouse, corporate IT.

Findings: 31 total. Critical 2, High 6, Medium 14, Low 9.

Critical
C1. Admin console: an IDOR lets any support-role user view the billing details of any tenant by changing an ID in the URL. Exploited in test. No evidence of abuse in the last 90 days of logs, but logs are only retained for 90 days. Fix in progress. Owner: Admin team (Luis), target Oct 24.
C2. CI/CD: long-lived production deploy credentials are stored as plain CI variables, readable by any repo maintainer (approx 140 people). Owner: none assigned. Platform says it belongs to Security. Security says it's Platform's pipeline. Estimated 6 to 8 engineer-weeks to move all 37 pipelines to short-lived OIDC credentials.

High
H1. No rate limiting on the public API password reset endpoint. Owner: Identity, fixed Oct 3.
H2. Android app stores refresh tokens outside OS secure storage. Owner: Mobile, target Nov 15.
H3 to H6. Outdated dependencies with known CVEs in 4 services. Owners: respective service teams, no target dates set.

Medium and Low: listed in Appendix A. Mostly headers, verbose errors and session timeouts. Halvard rates them low likelihood.

Compared with last year: last year had 24 findings (Critical 1, High 5). 19 of those are closed. 5 Mediums remain open, two of them for more than 12 months.

Remediation estimate (Priya):
Critical: approx 9 engineer-weeks
High: approx 7 engineer-weeks
Medium/Low: approx 12 engineer-weeks
Total approx 28 engineer-weeks, roughly $210k at blended internal cost. As a dedicated project, Priya estimates completion by end of Q1. Spread across team roadmaps, she estimates Q3 based on past rates, but calls this a rough guess.

Compliance: our SOC 2 Type II audit window opens Jan 15. Auditors will ask about C2 specifically, because access control over production deploys is a tested control. Halvard could not say whether an open C2 with a remediation plan would be raised as an exception.

Halvard recommendations: assign an owner to C2 within 2 weeks, extend log retention to 1 year, set SLA targets by severity.

Appendix A: medium and low findings (23 rows, omitted)
---

Need an exec summary of this postmortem for the leadership team (CEO, CFO, CTO, VP Customer). They meet Monday 10/20 and need to agree whether to assign owners and dates to the open action items in that meeting, and whether to send a proactive note to affected customers.

Postmortem: Checkout outage, Oct 9
Author: Tomas Vidal (SRE). Reviewers: Hana Kim, Dev Patel
Status: draft, blameless

Summary
On Oct 9 from 14:12 to 15:58 UTC (1h46m), roughly 70% of checkout attempts on the Acme storefront failed with a payment error. A config change deployed at 14:05 cut the payment gateway connection pool from 200 to 20 max connections because of a typo. Under afternoon load the pool ran out and requests timed out.

Timeline (UTC)
14:05 config change deployed, passed pipeline checks
14:12 error rate starts rising
14:19 checkout error alert fires to payments on-call
14:31 on-call acknowledges (was on another incident bridge)
14:48 SEV1 declared
15:20 config change identified as likely cause
15:34 rollback starts. During business hours the pipeline requires a second approver, who took 14 minutes to join
15:58 error rate back to baseline

Impact
Failed checkout attempts: approx 41,000
Unique customers affected: approx 18,500
Estimated lost GMV: $1.1M to $1.6M. The range depends on how many customers retried later. Analytics is still reconciling, with a final figure expected Oct 24
Support tickets: 2,340 in 48 hours vs a typical 400
6 enterprise merchants contacted their account managers. One, Fabrikam Retail, has asked about SLA credits. Their contract allows up to a 10% monthly fee credit, and legal is reviewing whether this incident qualifies.
No data loss. No security impact.

What went poorly
Config values are not checked against sane ranges. 12 minutes passed between the alert and acknowledgement. The rollback approval rule added delay during an outage. Finding the cause took 32 minutes after the SEV1 was declared, because config deploys don't appear on the incident dashboard.

Root cause
A manually edited config value with no range validation, deployed without a canary.

Action items
1. Range validation for connection pool config. Owner: Payments (Dev Patel). Due Oct 31.
2. Show config deploys on the incident dashboard. Owner: SRE (Hana Kim). Due Nov 14.
3. Single-approver rollback during declared incidents. Owner: TBD (pipeline shared by Platform and Release Eng). Due: TBD.
4. Canary deploys for config changes. Owner: TBD. Due: TBD. Est. 3 to 4 weeks of work.
5. Escalation when the primary on-call is on another incident. Owner: SRE (Hana Kim). Due: not set.
6. Customer communication and credits approach. Owner: not assigned (possibly VP Customer). Due: not set.

Open question
Was the 14:05 change reviewed? The PR shows one approval, but the reviewer doesn't remember approving it.
---
